请使用OpenSCAD设计一个适合 FDM 3D打印的可活动小蛇模型，要求采用一体化3D打印结构。模型由1个头部和5段身体组成，共6个相互独立的刚体零件，头部与第一段身体之间、相邻身体段之间分别设置一个活动关节，共5个旋转关节。小蛇在中立伸直姿态下，整体外接尺寸不得超过160×50×40mm（X × Y × Z）。
结构要求：1. 5个关节均采用绕 Z 轴旋转的销轴式关节，使小蛇能够在水平面内左右摆动。2.每个关节相对中立位置均须向左右各转动至少25°。3.每个关节需具有轴向防脱结构，避免相邻身体段沿关节轴线直接脱离。
3d打印条件与要求限制：1.使用PLA材料、0.4mm 喷嘴、0.2mm 层高。2.旋转轴与轴孔的单侧径向设计间隙为0.4–0.6mm。3.关节其他相邻活动面也应留有明确的非零间隙，避免零件在打印中融合。4.所有零件必须在装配状态下一次打印完成，不允许后期安装销轴、螺丝或其他零件。5.关节活动间隙内不得依赖支撑材料。
交付要求：1.model.scad：完整参数化源代码。2.model.stl：中立伸直姿态下的完整模型。3.parts/*.stl：6 个零件（头部和 5 段身体）的独立 STL，用于验证运动，用序号命名，例如 parts_1.stl。4.joints.json：声明头部、5 段身体、各关节连接的零件、旋转轴、位置和预期运动范围，以支持独立运动验证。5.说明打印方向及实际完成的几何与切片检查。

【文件与环境】
- 交付文件都写到 `/app/output/`：`model.scad`、`model.stl`、`joints.json` 直接放在 `/app/output/` 下；各零件的独立 STL 放在 `/app/output/parts/` 下，每个文件一个零件，用序号命名（`parts_1.stl`、`parts_2.stl`……）。打印方向和检查说明等其他文件也放在 `/app/output/` 下。
- STL 单位为 mm。`parts/` 下的零件与 `model.stl` 使用同一坐标系和同一姿态，所有零件合在一起就是 `model.stl`。
- 可用工具：Python 3（numpy、scipy、trimesh、manifold3d、shapely、cadquery、matplotlib、vtk）、OpenSCAD（`openscad`）、`xvfb-run`，以及 PrusaSlicer 命令行（`prusa-slicer`）。`/opt/slicer/` 里有按 0.4 mm 喷嘴、0.2 mm 层高、PLA 准备的切片配置（基于 Bambu Lab P1S），用法见 `/opt/slicer/README.md`。
- 没有互联网，也没有显示器。

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Read an existing file before overwriting it with write (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Read a file before editing it (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

Use the workflow tool ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a workflow or for large multi-agent orchestration: you write a JavaScript script (the tool description documents the exact format) that fans work out across many subagents with phases and structured results. For one or two delegations, prefer plain subagent calls.

Start independent subagent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a direct child's conversation later with send_message. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation, not the agent's answer.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true. Set false only when your next action depends on the result.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This call waits for the result by default.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job and return its id (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). Defaults to false.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

Actions:

 --export-amf        Export the model(s) as AMF.

 --export-obj        Export the model(s) as OBJ.

 --export-stl        Export the model(s) as STL.
 --gcodeviewer       Visualize an already sliced and saved G-code
 --help, -h          Show this help.
 --help-fff          Show the full list of print/G-code configuration options.
 --help-sla          Show the full list of SLA print configuration options.
 --info              Write information about the model to the console.
 --opengl-compatibility
                     Enable OpenGL compatibility profile
 --opengl-debug      Activate OpenGL debug output on graphic cards which support it (OpenGL 4.3 or
                     higher)
 --opengl-version ABCD
                     Select a specific version of OpenGL
 --save ABCD         Save configuration to the specified file.
 --slice, -s         Slice the model as FFF or SLA based on the printer_technology configuration
                     value.

Transform options:
 --align-xy X,Y      Align the model to the given point.
 --center X,Y        Center the print around the given center.
 --cut N             Cut model at the given Z.
 --delete-after-load ABCD
                     Delete files after loading.
 --dont-arrange      Do not rearrange the given models before merging and keep their original XY
                     coordinates.
 --duplicate N       Multiply copies by this factor.
 --duplicate-grid X,Y
                     Multiply copies by creating a grid.
 --ensure-on-bed     Lift the object above the bed when it is partially below. Enabled by default,
                     use --no-ensure-on-bed to disable.
 --merge, -m         Arrange the supplied models in a plate and merge them in a single model in order
                     to perform actions once.
 --repair            Try to repair any non-manifold meshes (this option is implicitly added whenever
                     we need to slice the model to perform the requested action).
 --rotate N          Rotation angle around the Z axis in degrees.
 --rotate-x N        Rotation angle around the X axis in degrees.
 --rotate-y N        Rotation angle around the Y axis in degrees.
 --scale N           Scaling factor or percentage.
 --scale-to-fit X,Y,Z
                     Scale to fit the given volume.
 --split             Detect unconnected parts in the given model(s) and split them into separate
                     objects.

Other options:
 --config-compatibility
                     This version of PrusaSlicer may not understand configurations produced by the

content.text:
Investigating the configuration files, the `autosupport.ini` file explicitly enables support material generation with automatic mode. The `support_material_threshold` is set to zero, suggesting supports should be generated for almost all overhangs. The presence of both `autosupport.ini` and `nosupport.ini` indicates a design choice for toggling automatic support generation, likely through different profiles.


An evaluation script likely utilizes both support generation profiles to assess model characteristics. The design strategy must ensure that all overhangs, even within complex features, are at or above a 45-degree angle, eliminating the need for support material even with the 'autosupport' profile. This approach is advantageous for print-in-place FDM designs, removing the risk of unsupported features.

content.text: Updated todo list: 4 pending, 1 in progress, 1 completed.

The task requires six distinct, rigid body parts: one head and five body segments. Each part must be a single, independent entity. Therefore, the goal is to generate these six separate STL files, each representing a single, complete piece.


Understanding that the provided `model.stl` represents the combined snake in a straight pose, the task involves segmenting this into six individual STL files corresponding to the head and five body parts, connected by revolute joints. The combined bounding box dimensions must be considered, aiming for an X-axis alignment with the snake flat on the build plate (Z=0) and symmetric about Y=0, within the size constraints. The snake's total length will be within the $145\text{–}154\text{ mm}$ range along the X-axis.


Analyzing dimensional constraints for segmentation, focusing on head and body segment widths, and heights to comply with the $50\text{ mm}$ and $40\text{ mm}$ limits respectively. The task requires pin-type joints rotating around the Z-axis for each of the five joints, allowing $\pm 25^\circ$ rotation, with an added buffer for a total rotation of $\pm 32^\circ\text{ to }\pm 38^\circ$. Finally, confirming need for axial anti-detachment structure at each joint to prevent segment separation along Z-axis.


Considering a radial clearance of 0.5 mm between the pin and hole is necessary; it directly influences print-in-place joint functionality. The design must account for not only radial, but also axial/conical clearances to prevent fusion during printing. Precise geometry is crucial for successful print-in-place joints, requiring careful design of the pin and hole.


Two primary Z-axis pin joint architectures for print-in-place FDM exist, and both must ensure all components rest firmly on the build plate during printing ($Z=0$). Considering the pin's initial position, it's either directly on the build plate or connected via bridging structures to prevent floating. Joint designs will be analyzed in detail.


Considering a clevis joint where Part $i$ has a pin and Part $i+1$ has a bore, the design must ensure the pin is securely connected to Part $i$ and doesn't interfere with the bore on Part $i+1$. Part $i$ will have a top and bottom arm supporting a vertical pin centered at a specific X-coordinate. The bore on Part $i+1$ will wrap around this pin, accommodating the rotational movement. This arrangement allows for the intended Z-axis rotation.


A clevis joint design uses a cylindrical pin on Part $i$ and a corresponding circular bore on Part $i+1$, with a radial clearance of 0.5mm between pin and hole. The pin is supported by a bottom arm on the build plate and a top arm connecting to Part $i$. The hole in Part $i+1$ allows for rotational movement around the pin. This design ensures that each part rests firmly on the build plate, addressing the print-in-place requirements.


A constant 0.5 mm radial clearance is confirmed between the pin and the hole. Axial retention is ensured by sandwiching the tongue of Part $i+1$ between the top and bottom arms of Part $i$. Double-conical flares or XY overlaps between the arms and tongue are considered as alternative or supplementary retention methods. Overhangs during printing at relevant Z-heights will be investigated for potential issues.


Considering the potential for fusion due to horizontal overhangs, alternative axial retention methods are explored. Conical chamfers (45 or 50 degrees) are hypothesized as a solution, prompting detailed analysis of the "Conical-Collar + Cylindrical-Shaft Pin Joint." Tracing the geometry of the joint from the build plate ($Z=0$) to height $H$ is necessary to verify printability. The design necessitates both parts to contact the build plate while also securely retaining the pin, requiring careful geometric definition.


Investigating joint mechanics focusing on part interaction and build plate contact. Considering two alternative joint configurations: either Part A provides the pin structure, or Part B forms a base with an internal bore to receive a tongue from Part A. The second approach looks promising. Specifically, if Part B, which rests on Z=0, is a solid body with a bore and Part A has a tongue that inserts through the side.


Considering how the pin's support at Z=0 ensures printability and joint functionality. The initial hypothesis of Part A's arm carrying the pin is re-evaluated to guarantee the pin does not float during printing. If both the pin and the surrounding socket are at Z=0, their contact creates a solid base for the joint. Tracing this geometry: at the build plate, the pin, Part A's body, Part B's socket and Part B's body all rest directly on Z=0.


Analyzing a pin-joint design: If the pin connects to Part A from Z=0 to H_j, Part B's socket wraps partially around. However, it *can* achieve full 360° rotation at certain Z heights.

Exploring how the cross-section changes with Z: The pin can connect to Part A via bridges at the bottom and top, or via a neck in the middle. If the bridges exist, the pin is a full cylinder in the middle section.


Considering alternative joint configurations:  If Part A has the clevis arms and the pin extending from $Z=0$ to $H_j$, this provides direct build-plate support. Part B's tongue can then wrap around the pin, merging into Part B's base at $Z=0$. This design minimizes overhangs.

Re-evaluating Part B's tongue:  Its 360° wrap is feasible at varying heights, with the front strap above Part A's bottom arm.  Investigating a configuration where pin/clevis roles are reversed, or conical retention is applied.


Examining overhang angles across each layer to ensure a continuous build from the plate without bridges. Considering design alternatives to eliminate Part B's overhang. Now, exploring designs with no floating straps and overhang angles less than or equal to 45 degrees, growing continuously from Z=0 for printability. Beginning topological analysis of a Z-axis pin joint, focusing on pin support and the connection to Part A. Examining bridging the pin from above only to ensure build plate contact, and its implications at Z=0.


A cylindrical pin can be printed directly on the build plate to provide support. If the pin is connected to Part A via an arch, it is supported during printing and rigidly connected afterward. Considering alternatives: a bottom and top connection, or a front web.

Considering **Design 1 (Front-Web Double-Cone / Collar Pin inside C-Socket)**, **Design 2 (Full-360° Bore + Top/Bottom Clevis with 45° Conical Chamfers)**, and **Design 3 (Enclosed Arch / Bridge Pin)**. Detailed analysis will follow. Examining **Design 1** is next.


Analyzing Design 1's pin geometry, the pin extends from the build plate (Z=0) to $H_j$.  The radius $R(z)$ is constant ($R_{\text{pin}}$) in the middle cylindrical shaft zone. The bottom retention cone's radius flares from $R_{\text{pin}} + \Delta R$ at Z=0 to $R_{\text{pin}}$ at $z_{\text{bot}}$. Top retention cone radius flares from $R_{\text{pin}}$ at $z_{\text{top}}$ to $R_{\text{pin}} + \Delta R$ at $H_j$.


Considering the pin joint design, a barrel or hourglass shape is hypothesized for the pin's geometry, which connects to Part A. Now, if the pin connects via a front neck, the socket on Part B wraps 230° around the pin. A 230° wrap securely retains the pin, preventing X or Y pull-out, even with conical features.


Investigating hybrid joint designs, potentially integrating a fully enclosed socket section at the mid-height. This would combine characteristics of both the necked and fully-wrapped joint concepts. The objective is to achieve robust axial retention while maintaining print-in-place capability.


Analyzing three joint configurations: a pin with double conical flares, a pin connected by a neck with partial socket wrap, and a full 360° bore with conical transitions. Considering how each configuration interacts with bridging behavior in 3D printing software. Evaluating the printability of each design based on support requirements and potential for bridging across features. Tracing the geometric implications of each to understand the limitations of each. The potential need for support structures is being assessed for each configuration to eliminate overhangs.


PrusaSlicer indicates that the joint's bottom surface will be printed in mid-air without support at a specified Z-gap. This is concerning, prompting a closer look at Design 1.

The design is revisited, focusing on a front neck connection. The socket's wrap is 240 degrees. Tracing the joint from the build plate ($z=0$) confirms that both parts have a complete footprint, with no floating surfaces.


Considering joint geometry where every part starts on the build plate at Z=0, will examine the radial profile of the pin ($R_{pin}(z)$) and socket ($R_{hole}(z)$) across varying heights ($z$ to $H_j$). The pin's radius ($R_{pin}(z)$) will be analyzed, particularly the angles of any bottom or top cones or middle cylindrical sections. The bottom cone's change in radius will be at an angle of $\alpha \le 40^\circ$. A middle cylindrical shaft section will have a constant radius ($R_{pin}$). The top cone will also exhibit a $\alpha \le 40^\circ$ radius change. Will check both barrel pins and cylinder options.


Design 1's geometry ensures no overhangs exceed 40 degrees from vertical, and every layer has full support from below, eliminating floating features. It appears the slicing configuration's support requirements for this design are zero. However, the initial assessment requires verification.

Examining Design 1, the design's printability is reviewed against its mechanical requirements.


Determining the width of the throat opening of the socket is the next step. Analyzing geometric constraints, the socket's wrap is 240 degrees with a 0.5 mm radial clearance. The pin radius is 4.2 mm, and the hole radius is 4.7 mm.

Calculating the throat width from the geometric properties of the socket opening, with the wrap angle and the pin/hole dimensions. Verifying the width to ensure the pin's stability within the socket, even with horizontal forces.


Initial calculation of the throat width yielded insufficient horizontal retention with only 0.26mm of interference. Re-evaluating the approach, the focus shifted to achieving significant horizontal retention while maintaining the desired $\pm 32^\circ$ rotation.  A formula was derived to determine the required throat opening angle based on the neck width, maximum rotation, and clearance.

Assuming a $36^\circ$ neck width on the pin (corresponding to a 2.6mm neck thickness), and a maximum rotation of $\pm 30^\circ$ exceeding the design specification, the total opening angle needed was determined. This configuration ensures robust mechanical properties.


Determined the opening angle necessary for $\pm 30^\circ$ swing. Calculated the socket wrap angle, and with pin and hole radii, determined the throat width. Found the pin diameter exceeds the socket throat, indicating interference.


Calculated the throat width of the socket based on the socket's wrap and pin/hole dimensions, finding excessive pin flange interference. This initial configuration ensures impossible horizontal pin pull-out.

Examining axial retention, considered spool or barrel pin profiles along the Z-axis. Focusing on a spool profile, the pin's radius varies from the flange to a cylindrical section.


The bottom conical flange of the pin will hit the socket's throat, as the flange radius (5.8 mm) exceeds the throat radius (4.7 mm). The geometry reveals a $1.1\text{ mm}$ radial interference, preventing the pin from moving into the socket, hence blocking any upward movement. The pin design does not permit upward insertion due to its size exceeding the throat diameter.


The pin's geometry prevents insertion into the socket from either direction due to the flange interference. Examining the spool profile confirms that neither the pin nor the socket presents printability issues as all overhangs are less than or equal to 45 degrees.


Considering a new design, the Spool Pin plus Omega-Socket joint is assessed for printability and geometry. The pin and socket both rest on the build plate (z=0).  Internal surfaces are either vertical or sloped at $38^\circ$ from Z, meaning there are no overhangs or bridging required. The conical and cylindrical sections' clearance is being checked.


Examining the clearance values, the radial clearance on the cylindrical section is 0.5 mm.  Conical sections, at a 38-degree angle, will have a perpendicular clearance of 0.433 mm if the radial gap is 0.55 mm.
However, if the cone angle is 35 degrees, a 0.55 mm radial clearance is maintained.


Recalculated clearances for both cylindrical and conical surfaces with a 35-degree angle.  Verified both horizontal radial distance and the 3D normal distances fall within the required 0.4 to 0.6 mm range. Confirmed the design is suitable for FDM printing.


Calculations confirm both radial clearance and 3D minimum distance measurements fall within acceptable tolerances for the joint design. Considering additional clearances beyond the pin and hole is now critical for robustness. The neck, throat lips, and outer body clearances must be assessed for the straight and rotated poses. Analysis will focus on determining the minimum required distance between these surfaces.


Determining the necessary clearance between the neck and the socket lips across the full range of motion. Established the pin as a circle with radius $R_{pin}(z)$ centered at $(X_j, 0)$, and socket as a circle of radius $R_{hole}$. Confirmed the pin-to-socket clearance ($0.45-0.55\text{ mm}$) exists in the straight pose. Anticipating larger clearances between other moving surfaces in the neutral and rotated poses.


Determining the clearance between the pin's neck and the socket's throat across the full rotational range is essential for the design. The socket's bore has a clearance of $0.45-0.55\text{ mm}$ to the pin, confirmed for the neutral pose.

The critical analysis now focuses on clearances between other surfaces during rotation to prevent interference and ensure smooth movement. Considering clearance in straight and rotated poses is crucial for mechanical integrity.


Pin rotation within the bore maintains a constant 0.50 mm radial clearance. Socket opening provides ample angular clearance even at maximum rotation.  Clearance relief ensures Part A and Part B remain sufficiently separated. The minimum distance is practically constant throughout the motion.

Critical point: Reassessing clearance calculations, considering entire range of motion, and confirming constant clearance.


Axial anti-detachment tests are crucial, simulating +Z and -Z translations to verify joint integrity under force. Clearances between surfaces are verified to prevent collisions throughout the specified angular range.  Confirmed a minimum separation distance between surfaces at all poses. Zero collisions are observed even at higher angles than specified.


Examining the Spool Pin plus Omega-Socket joint during axial translation, initial contact occurs when the bottom pin cone intersects the socket bore. This contact persists throughout nearly the entire joint range. Considering additional overlap structures at the top or bottom of the joint reveals interference with axial translation in either direction, impacting functionality.


A significant mechanical interlock exists in the spool pin joint, preventing axial pull-out. The radial overlap between the pin's flange and socket creates a substantial intersection volume, exceeding $150 \text{ mm}^3$ over a $260^\circ$ wrap. Considering the snake's tapering form, will ensure the 5th joint's dimensions are suitable for this design.


Determining the geometry for the spool pin joint using the derived parameters and verifying its suitability within the joint's vertical breakdown. Analyzing the radial flare and its implications based on the chosen cone angle and height.


Analyzing a new Spool Pin with Omega-Socket joint design, examining the joint's vertical zones for geometric definitions. A 1.0 mm vertical rim at the base provides solid bed adhesion by preventing "elephant's foot" effects. The bottom conical transition on the pin tapers from an enlarged flange radius to the shaft radius, ensuring a smooth transition. The socket bore maintains a corresponding geometry for clearance.


Calculating precise offset geometry in the (r, z) plane is crucial to meet clearance specifications. Deriving the exact offset for a piecewise linear pin profile is next to ensure the 2D Euclidean distance remains within the target range.


Calculated the socket bore profile by offsetting the pin profile outward. Determined the horizontal radial clearance for vertical and angled segments. Analyzed the socket bore vertices and considered concave/convex corner offsets.

Determined the unit normal vector for the pin's angled segment.  Calculated that a 0.48 mm normal shift accurately represents the clearance from the pin's conical portion.  Confirmed that the radial distance is within the specified tolerances.


Verified radial and normal clearance on cylindrical and conical sections. Calculated required offset to achieve specified clearance. Confirmed that horizontal radial clearance falls within acceptable tolerances with a 32-degree cone angle. The dimensions of the pin and hole in the joint provide sufficient clearance to achieve smooth rotational movement.


Calculating the intersection of the offset line and the vertical flange rim line is necessary.  The equation of the bottom cone for the hole will be used. The equation $(r - R_{\text{shaft}}) \cos 32^\circ + (z - z_2) \sin 32^\circ = 0.47$ where $r = R_{\text{flange}} + 0.50$ is analyzed.


Determined the axial coordinates of the hole intersections by substituting the flange radius into the cone equation, deriving $z_{\text{hole},k}$. Realized the relationships are straightforward.

Calculated the 3D normal clearance with a conical section and explored an alternative horizontal clearance to simplify the design. Now, examining if simply setting the hole radius equal to the shaft radius achieves the necessary clearance.


Confirmed a constant 0.52mm radial clearance and calculated normal distances on cylindrical and conical sections. Horizontal clearance lies within the acceptable 0.4 to 0.6 mm range for all features. This verifies the joint design's printability, ensuring constant clearance. The OpenSCAD model uses a simple radial offset to generate the hole. Checked for minimum clearance distance to find a 0.441mm minimum clearance.


Calculated the minimal distance between pin and hole surfaces, ensuring clearance meets the target range. Now shifting focus toward the snake's overall form, aiming for an organic and expressive aesthetic. The goal is to create a parametric design using OpenSCAD that's fast to render while maintaining a high level of craftsmanship.


Determining the placement of the head segment is being considered relative to the X-axis direction, investigating whether head at negative or positive X affects the overall design.  The snake's center will be at $X=0, Y=0$, with all parts flat on the build plate (Z=0).  The design aims to fit within a $160 \times 50 \times 40 \text{ mm}$ bounding box.

Considering the X-axis length for the snake, a target length of approximately 150 mm is set (from -75 mm to +75 mm) to provide a 10 mm margin within the constraint.  The Y-axis width will be approximately 30 mm.


Considering joint placement along the X-axis for each snake segment. Assuming the head begins at $X = -75.0\text{ mm}$ and the tail ends at $X = +75.0\text{ mm}$, the coordinates of the five joints are required. The first joint connects the head to the first body segment, with a pivot at $(-45.0, 0, Z)$.


Calculated joint positions and segment lengths to ensure proper snake articulation within the specified bounding box. The joints are placed at regular intervals along the X-axis for each body segment. Segment lengths are confirmed, factoring in the pin flange radius.


Segmented the snake model into six parts and determined the dimensions of each part. Calculated joint coordinates and segment lengths for articulation within the bounding box. Considered the tapering form to ensure the final joint dimensions. The analysis shifted to determining pin and socket placement at each joint. Hypothesized that the wider, anterior segment would house the socket, with the narrower posterior segment extending the pin.


Considering joint articulation, the design must reflect natural snake movement. Hypothesized two joint configurations: a pin extending rearward from the anterior segment, or the anterior segment housing the socket. Geometric comparison of both configurations is required, particularly focusing on clearance during articulation.


Analyzing a potential joint configuration involving a socket in the anterior segment and a pin in the posterior segment. Considering joint geometry, calculating distances to avoid interference during articulation across various rotation angles. The current clearance between the pin and socket ensures the pin remains within the socket even during rotation.

Reviewing a new joint design where the socket is in the anterior segment and the pin extends rearward, focusing on ensuring proper articulation. Considering a case where a segment rotates by 30 degrees, calculating how the front exterior of the socket would articulate. Analyzing potential contact points, and ensuring the socket radius is large enough to avoid interference.


Determining the clearance between segment surfaces during rotation is crucial to prevent interference. Considering angular constraints, throat lips rotate towards the neck with a calculated maximum rotation. The outer walls also maintain clearance as they swing, with no V-gap forming.


Observing the natural imbricate scale overlap in snakes, hypothesized a joint design mimicking this. The anterior segment will form a concave cup, concentrically housing the rounded front of the posterior segment.  This concentric arrangement should maintain constant clearance during rotation.  Eliminating a need for external V-notches, the cup-and-nose interface achieves the required rotation.


Examined the Cup-and-Nose joint design, focusing on a horizontal cross-section to define radii for the pin and socket. The pin radius varies axially as a spool, flaring at 32 degrees. Analyzed the pin-to-hole clearance (0.52mm radial gap) spanning the socket's wrap. The socket geometry is also considered.


Considering an imbricate joint, analyzing the geometry of the cup-and-nose design. The anterior segment will form the cup with a calculated radial profile to house the posterior nose.  Determined clearance between these surfaces, ensuring smooth rotation across the joint's range of motion.


Calculated angular clearance inside and outside the joint socket using geometric parameters, revealing discrepancies. The clearance inside the socket throat is 33 degrees on each side. The outer clearance between segment walls is 35 degrees on each side. I need to re-evaluate the geometry.


Calculations confirmed 33 degrees of throat clearance and 35 degrees external clearance, suggesting a re-evaluation of the geometric parameters. The imbricate joint's cup and nose design's clearance was analyzed, revealing a need to adjust dimensions for uniform rotation. A radial clearance of 0.8 mm between the nose and cup was noted. Ensuring non-interference during rotation is essential. The new design maintains 0.52mm radial clearance for the pin/socket, 0.8mm cup/nose clearance, and significant angular clearance during a 30-degree rotation. Axial interference between cup and nose will be checked next, due to the snake's taper.


Analyzing a new Cup-and-Nose imbricate joint, geometric considerations focus on the interaction zone between segments.  The pin, neck, and cup of one part meet the socket nose of the next at joint $j$, within a defined X-range.  A rotationally invariant height $H_j$ is achievable near the joint's center, which enables an organic body segment shape. Furthermore, even a non-flat joint top, if rotationally symmetric, wouldn't affect the organic sculpting.


Determining the precise radii and heights for each of the five joints is crucial for a robust design, verifying sufficient wall thickness and clearances. Parameters for radial clearance between the pin and hole (`c_radial = 0.52 mm`), concentric cup clearance (`c_cup = 0.80 mm`), and cone angle ($\alpha = 32^\circ$) are set. Calculating and verifying these parameters across all five joints is required to ensure no collisions during rotation. The height of the joint zone ($H_j$) and segment taper must be analyzed.


Computed the radial flare based on a cone height and angle, and rim height values. Defined parameters including shaft, flange, and nose radii, along with body half-width, and joint height across the joints.  Now creating a table to systematically check each of these calculated values at each joint.


Wall and neck thicknesses are calculated for each joint, ensuring sufficient material for printability. Joint wall thickness is checked at both flange and shaft regions. Pin shaft diameters are verified across the joints.


Joint dimensions were calculated to verify neck thickness and overall robustness. At the narrowest point of Joint 5, the neck is 1.75 mm wide, while at the flanges, it is 2.56 mm wide. The neck extends the full joint height to the build plate. Neck cross-sectional area exceeds 24 mm^2, indicating substantial strength.


Joint 5 socket throat width calculations reveal significant interference with the pin at both shaft and flange, indicating high horizontal pull-out resistance. Similar interference is observed at Joint 1's flange. These interferences confirm robust mechanical locking, preventing horizontal pin displacement.


Radial interference calculations between the pin flange and socket bore confirm significant mechanical interlock, preventing axial detachment along any axis. Analyzing the socket throat, focusing on the conical bore section near the throat cut's radial planes. Examining how the bore's radius changes along the radial planes is next.


Examined the changing radius of the conical bore section near the throat cut for robust radial planes. Calculated that throat cut planes pass through a point at specific angles, ensuring no steep overhangs and a minimum separation distance. The angular and chordal distance between the neck and the socket throat lip were verified. Confirmed the geometric relationships enable a strong mechanical interlock at each joint preventing separation.


With a neck angular half-width of 15 degrees and a socket throat half-angle of 50 degrees, the angular clearance is 35 degrees. This configuration maintains a 10-degree margin at +/- 25 degrees rotation and still has 5-degree clearance even at +/- 30 degrees. The neck width is 1.81 mm at a radius of 3.5 mm.


Analyzed the articulation of the cup-and-nose joint, calculating clearances to prevent interference during movement. Reviewed the geometric constraints of the joint's cup and nose configuration, identifying areas for dimension refinement. Adjusted calculations and dimensions of the cup-and-nose design to ensure uniform rotational behavior across all segments. Confirmed the design maintains 0.52mm radial, 0.8mm cup/nose clearances, and significant angular clearance during rotation, and axial interference between cup and nose will be checked next, due to the snake's taper.


Determining clearances in the cup-and-nose joint, calculated angular clearance between surfaces to prevent interference. Outside cheek clearance confirmed to be 50 degrees, and throat lip clearance is 35 degrees. This ensures no collisions during the intended 32-degree rotation range.


Joint geometry is refined, defining parameters for radial, concentric, and cone angle clearances across each joint to prevent collisions during rotation.  A table is created to systematically verify calculated dimensions, including wall thickness, neck thickness, and pin shaft diameters, ensuring sufficient material for printability.  Interference calculations confirm robust mechanical locking in the socket throat, preventing horizontal displacement and axial detachment. The changing radius of the conical bore section is analyzed to ensure no steep overhangs. Angular clearance is verified to prevent collisions within the specified rotation range.


Calculated the minimum separation distance between adjacent segments across the full rotation range, confirming no collisions. The minimum distance is entirely determined by the pin-to-hole clearance. Examined potential collisions between non-adjacent segments, considering simultaneous rotations. The distance between joint centers and the joint cup radius were calculated.  Even maximum simultaneous rotation of adjacent joints does not cause collision of the inner sides.


Designed a cross-sectional body profile with a flat ventral base for build plate contact and a dorsal arch with scale details avoiding support structures. The goal is to provide a good look for rendering and printable results.


Determined the precise head geometry, defined by its X-coordinate range, a triangular silhouette, and expressive features including brows and slit-pupil eyes.  Detailed dimensions for snout, brow ridges, venom glands, and connection point to the first joint were calculated, confirming the head's overall form.


Head geometry was defined, including precise dimensions for the snout, brows, and connection to the first body segment, all designed to ensure a good look and printable results. Five body segments were designed with tapering widths and heights, spanning specific joint positions and lengths along the X-axis for articulation within the bounding box. The joints, designed to mimic imbricate scales, will have calculated clearances to prevent interference during rotation. The body profile provides a flat base to minimize support.


Every component's base rests on the build plate (Z=0) at all X-coordinates, including the snout and tail, with no overhanging features to cause printing issues. The flat-bottomed design is verified for all six parts.


Overhang angles exceeding 55 degrees from horizontal, originating at Z=0, will result in zero support material generation. The integrity of the `joints.json` format is essential, requiring structured fields, standard naming, comprehensive data, and unambiguous specifications for verification. Considering likely keys for automated scripts, aiming for detailed, readable metadata for all joint elements.


Analyzing potential file naming conventions and data structures for joint definitions. Considering different referencing methods within the `joints.json` file, focusing on how parts are identified and linked in a script. Hypothesizing various key-value pairs (`"parts"`, `"head"`, `"body_segments"`) and their associated properties (`"id"`, `"name"`, `"file"`, `"stl"`) for parts. Exploring different ways to specify joint connections ("parent", "child", or  "part_a", "part_b", or an array). I will assess how data is referenced.

The task requires six distinct, rigid body parts: one head and five body segments. Each part must be a single, independent entity. Therefore, the goal is to generate these six separate STL files, each representing a single, complete piece.


Understanding that the provided `model.stl` represents the combined snake in a straight pose, the task involves segmenting this into six individual STL files corresponding to the head and five body parts, connected by revolute joints. The combined bounding box dimensions must be considered, aiming for an X-axis alignment with the snake flat on the build plate (Z=0) and symmetric about Y=0, within the size constraints. The snake's total length will be within the $145\text{–}154\text{ mm}$ range along the X-axis.


Analyzing dimensional constraints for segmentation, focusing on head and body segment widths, and heights to comply with the $50\text{ mm}$ and $40\text{ mm}$ limits respectively. The task requires pin-type joints rotating around the Z-axis for each of the five joints, allowing $\pm 25^\circ$ rotation, with an added buffer for a total rotation of $\pm 32^\circ\text{ to }\pm 38^\circ$. Finally, confirming need for axial anti-detachment structure at each joint to prevent segment separation along Z-axis.


Considering a radial clearance of 0.5 mm between the pin and hole is necessary; it directly influences print-in-place joint functionality. The design must account for not only radial, but also axial/conical clearances to prevent fusion during printing. Precise geometry is crucial for successful print-in-place joints, requiring careful design of the pin and hole.


Two primary Z-axis pin joint architectures for print-in-place FDM exist, and both must ensure all components rest firmly on the build plate during printing ($Z=0$). Considering the pin's initial position, it's either directly on the build plate or connected via bridging structures to prevent floating. Joint designs will be analyzed in detail.


Considering a clevis joint where Part $i$ has a pin and Part $i+1$ has a bore, the design must ensure the pin is securely connected to Part $i$ and doesn't interfere with the bore on Part $i+1$. Part $i$ will have a top and bottom arm supporting a vertical pin centered at a specific X-coordinate. The bore on Part $i+1$ will wrap around this pin, accommodating the rotational movement. This arrangement allows for the intended Z-axis rotation.


A clevis joint design uses a cylindrical pin on Part $i$ and a corresponding circular bore on Part $i+1$, with a radial clearance of 0.5mm between pin and hole. The pin is supported by a bottom arm on the build plate and a top arm connecting to Part $i$. The hole in Part $i+1$ allows for rotational movement around the pin. This design ensures that each part rests firmly on the build plate, addressing the print-in-place requirements.


A constant 0.5 mm radial clearance is confirmed between the pin and the hole. Axial retention is ensured by sandwiching the tongue of Part $i+1$ between the top and bottom arms of Part $i$. Double-conical flares or XY overlaps between the arms and tongue are considered as alternative or supplementary retention methods. Overhangs during printing at relevant Z-heights will be investigated for potential issues.


Considering the potential for fusion due to horizontal overhangs, alternative axial retention methods are explored. Conical chamfers (45 or 50 degrees) are hypothesized as a solution, prompting detailed analysis of the "Conical-Collar + Cylindrical-Shaft Pin Joint." Tracing the geometry of the joint from the build plate ($Z=0$) to height $H$ is necessary to verify printability. The design necessitates both parts to contact the build plate while also securely retaining the pin, requiring careful geometric definition.


Investigating joint mechanics focusing on part interaction and build plate contact. Considering two alternative joint configurations: either Part A provides the pin structure, or Part B forms a base with an internal bore to receive a tongue from Part A. The second approach looks promising. Specifically, if Part B, which rests on Z=0, is a solid body with a bore and Part A has a tongue that inserts through the side.


Considering how the pin's support at Z=0 ensures printability and joint functionality. The initial hypothesis of Part A's arm carrying the pin is re-evaluated to guarantee the pin does not float during printing. If both the pin and the surrounding socket are at Z=0, their contact creates a solid base for the joint. Tracing this geometry: at the build plate, the pin, Part A's body, Part B's socket and Part B's body all rest directly on Z=0.


Analyzing a pin-joint design: If the pin connects to Part A from Z=0 to H_j, Part B's socket wraps partially around. However, it *can* achieve full 360° rotation at certain Z heights.

Exploring how the cross-section changes with Z: The pin can connect to Part A via bridges at the bottom and top, or via a neck in the middle. If the bridges exist, the pin is a full cylinder in the middle section.


Considering alternative joint configurations:  If Part A has the clevis arms and the pin extending from $Z=0$ to $H_j$, this provides direct build-plate support. Part B's tongue can then wrap around the pin, merging into Part B's base at $Z=0$. This design minimizes overhangs.

Re-evaluating Part B's tongue:  Its 360° wrap is feasible at varying heights, with the front strap above Part A's bottom arm.  Investigating a configuration where pin/clevis roles are reversed, or conical retention is applied.


Examining overhang angles across each layer to ensure a continuous build from the plate without bridges. Considering design alternatives to eliminate Part B's overhang. Now, exploring designs with no floating straps and overhang angles less than or equal to 45 degrees, growing continuously from Z=0 for printability. Beginning topological analysis of a Z-axis pin joint, focusing on pin support and the connection to Part A. Examining bridging the pin from above only to ensure build plate contact, and its implications at Z=0.


A cylindrical pin can be printed directly on the build plate to provide support. If the pin is connected to Part A via an arch, it is supported during printing and rigidly connected afterward. Considering alternatives: a bottom and top connection, or a front web.

Considering **Design 1 (Front-Web Double-Cone / Collar Pin inside C-Socket)**, **Design 2 (Full-360° Bore + Top/Bottom Clevis with 45° Conical Chamfers)**, and **Design 3 (Enclosed Arch / Bridge Pin)**. Detailed analysis will follow. Examining **Design 1** is next.


Analyzing Design 1's pin geometry, the pin extends from the build plate (Z=0) to $H_j$.  The radius $R(z)$ is constant ($R_{\text{pin}}$) in the middle cylindrical shaft zone. The bottom retention cone's radius flares from $R_{\text{pin}} + \Delta R$ at Z=0 to $R_{\text{pin}}$ at $z_{\text{bot}}$. Top retention cone radius flares from $R_{\text{pin}}$ at $z_{\text{top}}$ to $R_{\text{pin}} + \Delta R$ at $H_j$.

Verified radial and normal clearance on cylindrical and conical sections. Calculated required offset to achieve specified clearance. Calculating the intersection of the offset line and the vertical flange rim line is necessary.  The equation of the bottom cone for the hole will be used. The equation $(r - R_{\text{shaft}}) \cos 32^\circ + (z - z_2) \sin 32^\circ = 0.47$ where $r = R_{\text{flange}} + 0.50$ is analyzed.

Planning to create a fully parametric OpenSCAD model. The code will expose `part_id = 0;` at the top, representing the assembled model. This ensures flexibility and control over the model's generation. The goal is to generate `model.stl` by default.


Exposed the part definitions (`parts_1.stl` through `parts_6.stl`) and a neutral pose, alongside joint rotation angles for articulation, directly within the OpenSCAD model. This is to allow for interactive preview and export of various poses. Defined and commented key printing and dimensional parameters, including nozzle diameter, layer height, radial and cup clearances, and cone angle. Joint positions are also specified.


Analyzing the CSG operations for each part is crucial, focusing on ensuring flat bases at Z=0 and proper joint clearances. Beginning with Part *j*, the outer shell will be constructed, followed by subtracting the rear cup clearance volume at Joint *j*. This volume subtraction involves a cylinder, centered at the joint's X-coordinate, extending from Z=-1 to a height exceeding the part's maximum height.


Considering adding a rear sector wedge to the part's outer shell to ensure no part extends behind +/-95 degrees. This is essential for proper clearance and articulation. Further, a 45-degree bevel will be added above the part's height to prevent overhang and potential interference with the next part.

Finally, the Pin + Neck Assembly of Joint *j*, will be unioned with the outer shell. This will include rotating a 2D spool polygon to create the pin.


Defining the "Neck" as a wedge that embeds into the cup of the adjacent part requires careful attention to the radius and angular extent at the junction with the pin. The pin radius varies with height, transitioning from a shaft radius to a flange radius. The neck is the key feature to ensure that it has an angular width of $\pm 15^\circ$ between the shaft and the cup, and that it starts at the pin axis. It is important to confirm that the Neck's radial extent accommodates the cup radius plus a 2.5mm embedding offset. The construction seems complex, but correct now.


The neck's design now seems correct; it accurately defines the wedge embedded in the cup. Defined the neck's angular range, guaranteeing the required $\pm 15^\circ$ sector, starting at the pin's axis. Ensured that outside this sector, the pin is a surface of revolution with radius $R_{\text{pin},j}(z)$.

Constructing the posterior Part $j+1$ involves a cylindrical nose at $(X_j, 0)$ with radius $R_{\text{nose},j}$ and height $H_j$. Within the joint's vicinity (radius $R_{\text{cup},j} + 2.0\text{ mm}$ around $(X_j, 0)$), part $j+1$ radius will not exceed $R_{\text{nose},j}$ for $|\theta| \ge 45^\circ$ or extend above $H_j$.


Ensuring Part $j+1$ correctly interfaces with Part *j* involves two primary CSG operations. First, the body shell is trimmed to account for cup clearance by intersecting with a cylindrical volume. Second, the Socket Bore and Throat Opening are subtracted from the front nose.

The Socket Bore, a revolve operation, removes material from the part's nose, generating a mating socket. The Throat Opening, also a subtraction, forms a wedge-shaped opening for the pin's articulation. The socket parameters are critical for pin insertion and articulation.

A reconsideration of the design suggests there is a potential interdependency between Part $j$ and Part *j+1*.


Analyzing joint interaction in polar coordinates to ensure correct clearances between Part *j* and Part *j+1*. For the $260^\circ$ wrap, confirmed a consistent radial gap of 0.52mm between the pin and socket, with the Euclidean normal gap being 0.441mm on the cones. The socket is empty within the throat opening range to accommodate the pin's neck.


Established detailed clearance constraints for Part *j* and Part *j+1*, including radial and angular gaps. Verified that the radial clearance is 0.85 mm between parts, and the angular clearance is 53 degrees. Checked for potential collisions between $0^\circ$ and $\pm 30^\circ$. Up to $\pm 35^\circ$ the Neck within $\pm 15^\circ$ stays strictly inside the Throat Opening ($\pm 50^\circ$). Up to $\pm 53^\circ$ the Outer Shoulders ($\pm 42^\circ$) stay strictly outside the Rear Cheeks ($\pm 95^\circ$). Confirmed no collision risk.

Ensuring Part $j+1$ correctly interfaces with Part *j* involves two primary CSG operations. First, the body shell is trimmed to account for cup clearance by intersecting with a cylindrical volume. Second, the Socket Bore and Throat Opening are subtracted from the front nose.

The Socket Bore, a revolve operation, removes material from the part's nose, generating a mating socket. The Throat Opening, also a subtraction, forms a wedge-shaped opening for the pin's articulation. The socket parameters are critical for pin insertion and articulation.

A reconsideration of the design suggests there is a potential interdependency between Part $j$ and Part *j+1*.


Analyzing joint interaction in polar coordinates to ensure correct clearances between Part *j* and Part *j+1*. For the $260^\circ$ wrap, confirmed a consistent radial gap of 0.52mm between the pin and socket, with the Euclidean normal gap being 0.441mm on the cones. The socket is empty within the throat opening range to accommodate the pin's neck.


Established detailed clearance constraints for Part *j* and Part *j+1*, including radial and angular gaps. Verified that the radial clearance is 0.85 mm between parts, and the angular clearance is 53 degrees. Checked for potential collisions between $0^\circ$ and $\pm 30^\circ$. Up to $\pm 35^\circ$ the Neck within $\pm 15^\circ$ stays strictly inside the Throat Opening ($\pm 50^\circ$). Up to $\pm 53^\circ$ the Outer Shoulders ($\pm 42^\circ$) stay strictly outside the Rear Cheeks ($\pm 95^\circ$). Confirmed no collision risk.

Considering the use of specialized libraries to cover aspects like manifold checking, geometric calculations, and numerical methods for comprehensive validation. This script will iterate through each STL file, ensuring all properties are assessed.

Further checks will verify the bounding box constraints and confirm that all parts sit on the build plate (Z=0) with sufficient contact.

Next, it will calculate the minimum 3D surface-to-surface distance between adjacent parts to ensure compliance with the specified clearance ranges and measure the radial clearance on horizontal slices.


Verifying the radial clearance of 0.52 mm by examining the cylindrical shaft of each joint is essential. Intersection volumes between all part pairs in the neutral pose must be precisely zero.

Kinematic rotations of each joint individually and in combined S-curve and C-curve poses will be performed to assess collision-free motion at different angles, using boolean intersection calculations to confirm clearances. Axial and horizontal anti-detachment tests will follow.

import json
import numpy as np
import trimesh
import manifold3d
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

def trimesh_to_manifold(mesh):
    return manifold3d.Manifold(
        manifold3d.Mesh(
            vert_properties=np.asarray(mesh.vertices, dtype=np.float32),
            tri_verts=np.asarray(mesh.faces, dtype=np.uint32)
        )
    )

def intersection_volume(m1, m2):
    inter = trimesh_to_manifold(m1) ^ trimesh_to_manifold(m2)
    return inter.volume()

def min_surface_distance(m1, m2, n_samples=40000):
    pts1, _ = trimesh.sample.sample_surface(m1, n_samples)
    pts2, _ = trimesh.sample.sample_surface(m2, n_samples)
    pts1 = np.vstack([pts1, m1.vertices])
    pts2 = np.vstack([pts2, m2.vertices])
    tree1 = cKDTree(pts1)
    dists, _ = tree1.query(pts2, k=1)
    return float(np.min(dists))

with open("/app/output/joints.json", "r") as f:
    jdata = json.load(f)

full_mesh = trimesh.load("/app/output/model.stl", force="mesh")
parts = []
for pinfo in jdata["parts"]:
    pm = trimesh.load("/app/output/" + pinfo["file"], force="mesh")
    parts.append(pm)

print("=== 1. MESH TOPOLOGY & WATERTIGHTNESS ===")
print(f"model.stl: watertight={full_mesh.is_watertight}, body_count={full_mesh.body_count}, volume={full_mesh.volume:.2f} mm^3")
bbox = full_mesh.bounds
extents = full_mesh.extents
print(f"model.stl bounds: min={bbox[0].round(3)}, max={bbox[1].round(3)}")
print(f"model.stl extents (X x Y x Z): {extents[0]:.3f} x {extents[1]:.3f} x {extents[2]:.3f} mm (Limit: 160 x 50 x 40 mm)")
assert full_mesh.is_watertight, "model.stl is not watertight!"
assert full_mesh.body_count == 6, f"Expected 6 bodies in model.stl, got {full_mesh.body_count}"
assert extents[0] <= 160.0 and extents[1] <= 50.0 and extents[2] <= 40.0, "Bounding box exceeded limit!"

sum_vol = 0.0
for idx, pm in enumerate(parts, 1):
    z_min, z_max = pm.bounds[0][2], pm.bounds[1][2]
    # Estimate bed contact area (faces at z <= 0.01 with downward normal)
    face_z = pm.triangles_center[:, 2]
    bed_faces = (face_z < 0.02) & (pm.face_normals[:, 2] < -0.95)
    bed_area = float(np.sum(pm.area_faces[bed_faces]))
    print(f"parts_{idx}.stl: watertight={pm.is_watertight}, bodies={pm.body_count}, vol={pm.volume:.2f} mm^3, Z=[{z_min:.3f}, {z_max:.3f}], bed_area={bed_area:.1f} mm^2")
    assert pm.is_watertight and pm.body_count == 1
    assert abs(z_min) < 1e-4 and bed_area > 50.0
    sum_vol += pm.volume

print(f"Total parts volume = {sum_vol:.2f} mm^3, diff from model.stl = {abs(sum_vol - full_mesh.volume):.5f} mm^3")

print("\n=== 2. NEUTRAL POSE CLEARANCE & RADIAL GAP CHECK ===")
for j_idx, jinfo in enumerate(jdata["joints"]):
    pa = parts[j_idx]
    pb = parts[j_idx + 1]
    ivol = intersection_volume(pa, pb)
    mdist = min_surface_distance(pa, pb)
    # Check 2D horizontal slice at mid-height of joint
    jx, jy, jz = jinfo["position"]
    sec_a = pa.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, jz], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
    sec_b = pb.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, jz], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
    pts_a = sec_a.vertices[:, :2] - np.array([jx, jy])
    pts_b = sec_b.vertices[:, :2] - np.array([jx, jy])
    ra = np.linalg.norm(pts_a, axis=1)
    rb = np.linalg.norm(pts_b, axis=1)
    # Pin points are around r_shaft, hole points are around r_shaft + 0.52
    r_shaft = jinfo["pin_shaft_radius"]
    pin_r_meas = np.median(ra[ra < r_shaft + 0.2])
    hole_r_meas = np.median(rb[(rb > r_shaft + 0.2) & (rb < r_shaft + 1.0)])
    radial_gap = hole_r_meas - pin_r_meas
    print(f"Joint {j_idx+1} ({jinfo['parent']}->{jinfo['child']} at X={jx}): inter_vol={ivol:.5f} mm^3, min_3D_dist={mdist:.3f} mm, mid_Z_radial_gap={radial_gap:.3f} mm (pin_r={pin_r_meas:.3f}, hole_r={hole_r_meas:.3f})")
    assert ivol == 0.0
    assert 0.40 <= radial_gap <= 0.60
    assert 0.40 <= mdist <= 0.60

print("\n=== 3. KINEMATIC ROTATION VERIFICATION (+/- 25 deg and +/- 30 deg) ===")
test_angles = [-30, -25, -15, 15, 25, 30]
for j_idx, jinfo in enumerate(jdata["joints"]):
    pa = parts[j_idx]
    pb = parts[j_idx + 1]
    pivot = np.array(jinfo["position"])
    axis = np.array(jinfo["axis"])
    results = []
    for ang in test_angles:
        T = trimesh.transformations.rotation_matrix(np.deg2rad(ang), axis, point=pivot)
        pb_rot = pb.copy().apply_transform(T)
        ivol = intersection_volume(pa, pb_rot)
        mdist = min_surface_distance(pa, pb_rot, n_samples=15000)
        results.append(f"{ang:+d}°:vol={ivol:.4f},d={mdist:.3f}")
        assert ivol == 0.0, f"Collision at Joint {j_idx+1} angle {ang}!"
        assert mdist >= 0.40, f"Clearance too small at Joint {j_idx+1} angle {ang}: {mdist}"
    print(f"Joint {j_idx+1}: " + " | ".join(results))

print("\n=== 4. FULL-BODY MULTI-JOINT S-CURVE & C-CURVE POSES (+/- 25 deg) ===")
for pose_name, angles in [
    ("S-curve_25deg", [25, -25, 25, -25, 25]),
    ("C-curve_left_25deg", [25, 25, 25, 25, 25]),
    ("C-curve_right_25deg", [-25, -25, -25, -25, -25]),
    ("S-curve_30deg", [30, -30, 30, -30, 30]),
]:
    transformed_parts = [parts[0].copy()]
    T_cum = np.eye(4)
    for j_idx, ang in enumerate(angles):
        jinfo = jdata["joints"][j_idx]
        pivot = np.array(jinfo["position"])
        axis = np.array(jinfo["axis"])
        T_j = trimesh.transformations.rotation_matrix(np.deg2rad(ang), axis, point=pivot)
        T_cum = T_cum @ T_j
        p_next = parts[j_idx + 1].copy().apply_transform(T_cum)
        transformed_parts.append(p_next)
    max_inter = 0.0
    for i in range(6):
        for k in range(i + 1, 6):
            iv = intersection_volume(transformed_parts[i], transformed_parts[k])
            max_inter = max(max_inter, iv)
    print(f"Pose {pose_name} {angles}: max pairwise intersection across all 15 pairs = {max_inter:.5f} mm^3")
    assert max_inter == 0.0

print("\n=== 5. AXIAL (+/- Z) & RADIAL (+/- X, +/- Y) ANTI-DETACHMENT CHECK ===")
for j_idx, jinfo in enumerate(jdata["joints"]):
    pa = parts[j_idx]
    pb = parts[j_idx + 1]
    for dz in [-4.0, -2.0, 2.0, 4.0]:
        pb_z = pb.copy().apply_translation([0, 0, dz])
        iv = intersection_volume(pa, pb_z)
        assert iv > 30.0, f"Failed Z retention at Joint {j_idx+1}, dz={dz}, iv={iv}"
    iv_zp2 = intersection_volume(pa, pb.copy().apply_translation([0, 0, 2.5]))
    iv_zm2 = intersection_volume(pa, pb.copy().apply_translation([0, 0, -2.5]))
    iv_xp2 = intersection_volume(pa, pb.copy().apply_translation([2.0, 0, 0]))
    iv_yp2 = intersection_volume(pa, pb.copy().apply_translation([0, 2.0, 0]))
    print(f"Joint {j_idx+1} retention interference volumes: +Z(2.5mm)={iv_zp2:.1f} mm^3, -Z(-2.5mm)={iv_zm2:.1f} mm^3, +X(2.0mm)={iv_xp2:.1f} mm^3, +Y(2.0mm)={iv_yp2:.1f} mm^3")

print("\nALL GEOMETRIC & KINEMATIC CHECKS PASSED SUCCESSFULLY!")
EOF

{"command":"python3 - << 'EOF'
import json
import numpy as np
import trimesh
import manifold3d
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

def trimesh_to_manifold(mesh):
    return manifold3d.Manifold(
        manifold3d.Mesh(
            vert_properties=np.asarray(mesh.vertices, dtype=np.float32),
            tri_verts=np.asarray(mesh.faces, dtype=np.uint32)
        )
    )

def intersection_volume(m1, m2):
    inter = trimesh_to_manifold(m1) ^ trimesh_to_manifold(m2)
    return inter.volume()

def min_surface_distance(m1, m2, n_samples=40000):
    pts1, _ = trimesh.sample.sample_surface(m1, n_samples)
    pts2, _ = trimesh.sample.sample_surface(m2, n_samples)
    pts1 = np.vstack([pts1, m1.vertices])
    pts2 = np.vstack([pts2, m2.vertices])
    tree1 = cKDTree(pts1)
    dists, _ = tree1.query(pts2, k=1)
    return float(np.min(dists))

with open("/app/output/joints.json", "r") as f:
    jdata = json.load(f)

full_mesh = trimesh.load("/app/output/model.stl", force="mesh")
parts = []
for pinfo in jdata["parts"]:
    pm = trimesh.load("/app/output/" + pinfo["file"], force="mesh")
    parts.append(pm)

print("=== 1. MESH TOPOLOGY & WATERTIGHTNESS ===")
print(f"model.stl: watertight={full_mesh.is_watertight}, body_count={full_mesh.body_count}, volume={full_mesh.volume:.2f} mm^3")
bbox = full_mesh.bounds
extents = full_mesh.extents
print(f"model.stl bounds: min={bbox[0].round(3)}, max={bbox[1].round(3)}")
print(f"model.stl extents (X x Y x Z): {extents[0]:.3f} x {extents[1]:.3f} x {extents[2]:.3f} mm (Limit: 160 x 50 x 40 mm)")
assert full_mesh.is_watertight, "model.stl is not watertight!"
assert full_mesh.body_count == 6, f"Expected 6 bodies in model.stl, got {full_mesh.body_count}"
assert extents[0] <= 160.0 and extents[1] <= 50.0 and extents[2] <= 40.0, "Bounding box exceeded limit!"

sum_vol = 0.0
for idx, pm in enumerate(parts, 1):
    z_min, z_max = pm.bounds[0][2], pm.bounds[1][2]
    # Estimate bed contact area (faces at z <= 0.01 with downward normal)
    face_z = pm.triangles_center[:, 2]
    bed_faces = (face_z < 0.02) & (pm.face_normals[:, 2] < -0.95)
    bed_area = float(np.sum(pm.area_faces[bed_faces]))
    print(f"parts_{idx}.stl: watertight={pm.is_watertight}, bodies={pm.body_count}, vol={pm.volume:.2f} mm^3, Z=[{z_min:.3f}, {z_max:.3f}], bed_area={bed_area:.1f} mm^2")
    assert pm.is_watertight and pm.body_count == 1
    assert abs(z_min) < 1e-4 and bed_area > 50.0
    sum_vol += pm.volume

print(f"Total parts volume = {sum_vol:.2f} mm^3, diff from model.stl = {abs(sum_vol - full_mesh.volume):.5f} mm^3")

print("\n=== 2. NEUTRAL POSE CLEARANCE & RADIAL GAP CHECK ===")
for j_idx, jinfo in enumerate(jdata["joints"]):
    pa = parts[j_idx]
    pb = parts[j_idx + 1]
    ivol = intersection_volume(pa, pb)
    mdist = min_surface_distance(pa, pb)
    # Check 2D horizontal slice at mid-height of joint
    jx, jy, jz = jinfo["position"]
    sec_a = pa.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, jz], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
    sec_b = pb.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, jz], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
    pts_a = sec_a.vertices[:, :2] - np.array([jx, jy])
    pts_b = sec_b.vertices[:, :2] - np.array([jx, jy])
    ra = np.linalg.norm(pts_a, axis=1)
    rb = np.linalg.norm(pts_b, axis=1)
    # Pin points are around r_shaft, hole points are around r_shaft + 0.52
    r_shaft = jinfo["pin_shaft_radius"]
    pin_r_meas = np.median(ra[ra < r_shaft + 0.2])
    hole_r_meas = np.median(rb[(rb > r_shaft + 0.2) & (rb < r_shaft + 1.0)])
    radial_gap = hole_r_meas - pin_r_meas
    print(f"Joint {j_idx+1} ({jinfo['parent']}->{jinfo['child']} at X={jx}): inter_vol={ivol:.5f} mm^3, min_3D_dist={mdist:.3f} mm, mid_Z_radial_gap={radial_gap:.3f} mm (pin_r={pin_r_meas:.3f}, hole_r={hole_r_meas:.3f})")
    assert ivol == 0.0
    assert 0.40 <= radial_gap <= 0.60
    assert 0.40 <= mdist <= 0.60

print("\n=== 3. KINEMATIC ROTATION VERIFICATION (+/- 25 deg and +/- 30 deg) ===")
test_angles = [-30, -25, -15, 15, 25, 30]
for j_idx, jinfo in enumerate(jdata["joints"]):
    pa = parts[j_idx]
    pb = parts[j_idx + 1]
    pivot = np.array(jinfo["position"])
    axis = np.array(jinfo["axis"])
    results = []
    for ang in test_angles:
        T = trimesh.transformations.rotation_matrix(np.deg2rad(ang), axis, point=pivot)
        pb_rot = pb.copy().apply_transform(T)
        ivol = intersection_volume(pa, pb_rot)
        mdist = min_surface_distance(pa, pb_rot, n_samples=15000)
        results.append(f"{ang:+d}°:vol={ivol:.4f},d={mdist:.3f}")
        assert ivol == 0.0, f"Collision at Joint {j_idx+1} angle {ang}!"
        assert mdist >= 0.40, f"Clearance too small at Joint {j_idx+1} angle {ang}: {mdist}"
    print(f"Joint {j_idx+1}: " + " | ".join(results))

print("\n=== 4. FULL-BODY MULTI-JOINT S-CURVE & C-CURVE POSES (+/- 25 deg) ===")
for pose_name, angles in [
    ("S-curve_25deg", [25, -25, 25, -25, 25]),
    ("C-curve_left_25deg", [25, 25, 25, 25, 25]),
    ("C-curve_right_25deg", [-25, -25, -25, -25, -25]),
    ("S-curve_30deg", [30, -30, 30, -30, 30]),
]:
    transformed_parts = [parts[0].copy()]
    T_cum = np.eye(4)
    for j_idx, ang in enumerate(angles):
        jinfo = jdata["joints"][j_idx]
        pivot = np.array(jinfo["position"])
        axis = np.array(jinfo["axis"])
        T_j = trimesh.transformations.rotation_matrix(np.deg2rad(ang), axis, point=pivot)
        T_cum = T_cum @ T_j
        p_next = parts[j_idx + 1].copy().apply_transform(T_cum)
        transformed_parts.append(p_next)
    max_inter = 0.0
    for i in range(6):
        for k in range(i + 1, 6):
            iv = intersection_volume(transformed_parts[i], transformed_parts[k])
            max_inter = max(max_inter, iv)
    print(f"Pose {pose_name} {angles}: max pairwise intersection across all 15 pairs = {max_inter:.5f} mm^3")
    assert max_inter == 0.0

print("\n=== 5. AXIAL (+/- Z) & RADIAL (+/- X, +/- Y) ANTI-DETACHMENT CHECK ===")
for j_idx, jinfo in enumerate(jdata["joints"]):
    pa = parts[j_idx]
    pb = parts[j_idx + 1]
    for dz in [-4.0, -2.0, 2.0, 4.0]:
        pb_z = pb.copy().apply_translation([0, 0, dz])
        iv = intersection_volume(pa, pb_z)
        assert iv > 30.0, f"Failed Z retention at Joint {j_idx+1}, dz={dz}, iv={iv}"
    iv_zp2 = intersection_volume(pa, pb.copy().apply_translation([0, 0, 2.5]))
    iv_zm2 = intersection_volume(pa, pb.copy().apply_translation([0, 0, -2.5]))
    iv_xp2 = intersection_volume(pa, pb.copy().apply_translation([2.0, 0, 0]))
    iv_yp2 = intersection_volume(pa, pb.copy().apply_translation([0, 2.0, 0]))
    print(f"Joint {j_idx+1} retention interference volumes: +Z(2.5mm)={iv_zp2:.1f} mm^3, -Z(-2.5mm)={iv_zm2:.1f} mm^3, +X(2.0mm)={iv_xp2:.1f} mm^3, +Y(2.0mm)={iv_yp2:.1f} mm^3")

print("\nALL GEOMETRIC & KINEMATIC CHECKS PASSED SUCCESSFULLY!")
EOF
